title: The Summer of Sandpiper Point
premise: Petra Thornbury has spent ten years ghostwriting other people's lives, including the bestselling memoirs of her rival, Margot Vane—built on a cache of anonymous letters Petra once wrote to a stranger she loved and lost. When the letter's recipient, Elias Ward, moves in next door to Sandpiper Point, he begins piecing together that the woman who vanished from his life is the same ghost behind Margot's celebrated words. As Petra races to finish Margot's final manuscript before a deadline that will publicly cement the theft of her own story, she and Elias confront what each did with the truth: he stopped searching, she stopped signing her name. In the end, Petra publishes a small book under her own name on the same day Margot's memoir launches, choosing visibility over safety—and choosing Elias only after learning to forgive the person in the mirror.
about_author: Freya Crane is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's daughter who spent fifteen years writing other people's stories before claiming one of her own. She lives on a windswept peninsula where she collects unsent letters and insists the tide keeps better secrets than any archive.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Petra arrives at Sandpiper Point to ghostwrite the final chapters of Margot Vane's memoir, hiding her resentment behind professional calm. Her POV establishes her invisibility as armor. The emotional beat is unease: the cottage next door has new tenants, and something about the moving truck makes her chest tighten.

chapters.title: A Stranger With Familiar Hands
chapters.summary: Elias Ward introduces himself over a borrowed ladder and a spilled box of books—including a first edition Petra once inscribed to him under a false name. His POV reveals he moved here deliberately, following a paper trail of letters. The beat is electric recognition masked as politeness; neither admits they know.

chapters.title: Margot's Version
chapters.summary: Working from Margot's dictated pages, Petra recognizes her own letters quoted verbatim, repurposed as Margot's lived experience. Petra's POV; the beat is quiet fury and self-blame, since she signed away rights years ago for money and anonymity. She begins keeping a secret counter-manuscript at night.

chapters.title: Ten Summers of Letters
chapters.summary: Elias confronts Petra gently with the full correspondence, asking why she disappeared after the last unsigned letter. Her POV alternates memory and present as she deflects, terrified that confession means losing both the memoir advance and the last version of herself anyone believes. The beat is aching near-honesty interrupted by Margot's summons.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: A storm floods the beach and uncovers a time capsule the two buried as young lovers, forcing them to spend a stranded night trading truths. Dual POV. Elias admits he married someone else and failed; Petra admits she watched his wedding announcement and wrote anyway. The beat is raw intimacy—but she still hides the ghostwriting.

chapters.title: The Deadline
chapters.summary: Margot accelerates publication to bury a scandal, demanding Petra deliver the manuscript in two weeks and threatening legal ruin if the letters' true origin surfaces. Petra's POV; the beat is claustrophobic pressure as she realizes exposure could destroy Elias's reputation too, since he was named in the letters.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Elias discovers the counter-manuscript and realizes Petra has been writing their love story into Margot's book all along. His POV; hurt curdles into resolve—he urges her to publish under her own name, but she refuses, believing no one buys stories from ghosts. The beat is the first real rupture between them.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Alone, Petra rereads her earliest letter and finally sees how long she has punished herself for wanting to be seen. Her POV, interior and quiet: she drafts a confession essay titled 'Ghostwriter,' deciding the worst outcome—being truly known—is survivable. The beat is the turn inward that makes the climax possible.

chapters.title: Launch Day
chapters.summary: At Margot's glittering launch party, Petra stands when the memoir's most famous passage is read aloud and claims it, presenting her dated originals to the room. Climax; alternating POV. Margot threatens litigation, but public opinion and Elias's steady presence shift the ground. The beat is terror transfigured into liberation.

chapters.title: Signed, At Last
chapters.summary: Months later, Petra's own slim book sits beside Margot's in the shop window, and a settlement lets her keep her name on every future page. Her POV closes the arc: she signs a fresh letter to Elias—not anonymous this time—and walks it next door. The beat is earned peace: forgiveness given, identity claimed, second chance taken.
